public_rationale: Marcus is betting against Musk's forecast that AI could do anything any human can do within a year or two of 29 October 2024. The latest reading of that window ends on 30 October 2026, two days after the evaluation date. No event has settled it early. Evidence from July 2026 shows the best AI agent completed only 15.8% of real freelance projects at professional quality. That points toward Marcus, but a 'will not' forecast can only be scored once its deadline passes.
limitations: The deadline is only days after the evaluation date.
The RLI benchmark covers remote digital work only, not physical tasks.

our_interpretation: Marcus's implied forecast: by two years after Musk's 2024-10-29 remark, no AI will be able to do anything any human can do.
Deadline: the latest reasonable end of 'within the next year or two' is two years after the post, 2026-10-30.
The bet offer itself is not checkable. Only the implied forecast is graded.

Early resolution rule: the forecast is contradicted early if, before the deadline, credible evaluations show an AI system able to do essentially any task a human can do, including physical and long-horizon work. It can be supported only once the deadline passes.
criteria.support_condition: At 2026-10-30, AI systems still cannot do many tasks humans can do, as shown by public capability evaluations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: By 2026-10-30, credible evidence shows an AI system that can do anything any human can do.
